            Web Protection drawn as FortiWeb draws it, and Sentinel split between Settings and Operations. The Web Protection Profile, its exceptions and the Bot Mitigation, API, DoS and IP Protection dialogs follow the device's own layout (FortiWeb 7.6.8, re-read with the harvester): Edit Signature Policy with its ten classes, Signature Details in FortiWeb's three panes with an editable Threat Weight, the HTTP Protocol Constraints, Known Bots, Syntax and Web Shell tables taken from the device's build, and every selector with its list, + Create and an Edit entry pencil that opens the device's dialog. The FortiWeb catalog's child tables are measured (three wrong paths corrected), a create is cached and named in the Audit Log, Sentinel reads FortiWeb 7.6.8's word severities, and Settings › Sentinel keeps only the configuration while the rest moves to Operations › Sentinel.

            Changed

            • Settings → Sentinel holds only configuration; the rest is Operations › Sentinel. Operator rule: what is configured stays in Settings, everything else goes to Operations. Settings → AI → Sentinel keeps three panes — Settings (the form only), Context and Response policy. A new Sentinel sub-menu right below Monitoring (Operations of every device ADOM, and the Global block) holds the Incidents console, a new Overview (/sentinel/overview: health, recent decisions, the local CVE mirror with Sync now and manual CVE entry, the pipeline, the score bands and weights, and the ten-scenario demo lab), the Border blocklist and the Architecture. They used to be Settings panes (the console also a single entry under Global › Monitoring); the CVE mirror sat under Context and the decision log under Response policy. The sub-menu follows the old entry's rule: it is drawn only while Sentinel is configured. The decision log keeps its audience (config write).

            • Every FortiWeb selector the audit found as a text box gets its list. A render of every dialog of {device}'s build found 33 selectors drawn as text boxes; the harvester now reads the forms their code uses (a selector named by a map's values -- Threshold Based Detection's triggers --, a source object inside a ternary -- OAuth server --, a registry source whose data function takes its GUI API path -- Interface --, and typed factories such as createOauthServerSource("authz"); harvester 652de51 and later), and SATOM ties the GUI API lists to their cmdb twins (Interface, admin local and CA certificates, CRL; measured or named on {device}). A list FortiWeb filters by a row field is filtered the same way: OAuth server's request selectors offer only the requests of their type, a server-policy selector only the policies of its protocol (cache first; only those measured collections and fields).

            • Every section of the Web Protection Profile opens with working tables and lists. Request: "in Edit Custom Signature Group I cannot create more members ... do all this for every section of the web profile; put those Create at the top." An audit of the 39 selectors of the Web Protection Profile against {device} found: 35 of 98 tables with Create New had no member dialog (the crawl opens one only from a row it can click, so an empty Custom Signature Group stayed disabled). The harvester now reads each table's member dialog off its parent's code (harvester ed10cf2, ba0d24c, c7d31fb; packs kb-20261101.11 and .12): 102 of 106 on 7.6.8, the dialog templates the crawl never drew fetched from {device}'s own GUI (same build). Two catalog entries pointed at the wrong sub-table and are corrected, measured on {device} (waf/graphql-validation.policy/ graphql-rule-list, waf/site-publish-helper.policy/rule; the old .../rule-list answers the parent object). IP List's IP External now lists the external resources (measured alias of the GUI's list to system/external-resource; harvester e1da453, pack kb-20261101.13). In the dropdown, + Create sits at the top of the list.
            • Known Bots, Syntax Detection and Web Shell Detection open as FortiWeb draws them; the signature-class and HTTP-constraint tables come from the device's build. Request: "do it now ... finish everything and leave nothing pending." Those three dialogs are, for most of their content, a table FortiWeb draws by hand (categories of rows, each row the object's own Status / Action / Block Period / Severity / Threat Weight / Trigger Policy fields); SATOM drew only their two to six header fields. The harvester now reads such tables off each dialog's code, row by row (harvester 252027b, 7f9a652, f7b3888; knowledge packs kb-20261101.8 to .10), and SATOM draws them with the object's values: categories that fold, Block Period usable only for a block action, the warning FortiWeb shows for Client ID Block Period, threat-weight levels by name, a cell the build's schema does not carry read-only. Edit Signature Policy's classes and HTTP Protocol Constraints (and its exception rule) now come from the same tables of the device's build instead of two JSON files measured by hand, which are gone (on {device} 7.6.8 the extracted tables equal those files row for row). Per build: on 8.0.6 False Positive Mitigation is drawn where the device's class row carries fpm_cap (7.6.8: the two SQL Injection classes); a build whose template lacks a table takes the nearest build's and says which. The PII Detection Threshold's GUI name is mapped to its cmdb key (credit-card-detection-threshold), measured on {device} by writing it.
            • Reference selectors are FortiWeb's dropdown, with Edit entry on each entry. A selector whose GUI source declares per-entry edit (199 of 220 sources on 7.6.8) opens a list with a search box, an Edit entry pencil on each entry (it opens that entry's dialog in the panel) and + Create at its foot, keyboard included (arrows, Enter, Esc). The saved value is the same select as before.
            • Certificate selectors list what FortiWeb lists, filtered by key type. The Certificate Group dialog's RSA, DSA and ECDSA Certificate selectors were text boxes (the ECDSA one could not even be saved: it had no field name). FortiWeb lists the local certificates there filtered by key type (pkey_type 1 / 2 / 3), from its GUI API, whose rows carry that field while the cmdb rows SATOM caches do not. The harvester now extracts that filter (harvester bac5516, knowledge pack kb-20261101.7: 4 templates, only those fields; the ECDSA selector is ecc-cert), and SATOM reads the GUI API list and offers only the matching certificates (measured on {device} 7.6.8: RSA and ECC certificates in their own lists). A failed read leaves the list empty with the error, never every certificate; only that measured list and its two filter fields can be read this way. OCSP Stapling's Local Certificate and the server pool's certificates list the local certificates as FortiWeb does (unfiltered).
            • Threat Weight is editable in Signature Details. Request: "do everything you can that does not depend on something external." Until now SATOM showed a signature's Threat Weight read-only. It is now set the way FortiWeb's own pane does (PUT waf/signature.advanced.signature.score, measured on {device} 7.6.8 from its GUI bundle and then live: 7, 0 and the default -1 are stored as sent and read back). Only FortiWeb's seven levels are offered and accepted: the device answers a value outside them with HTTP 200 and stores another level (3 was stored as 6), so SATOM refuses anything else before it is sent and verifies every write by reading the signature back. The current value is read first, the write is recorded in the Audit Log (signature.score, with the before value and verify) and a level the device does not keep fails (signature.score.not_applied). The pane shows levels by name instead of the raw integer.
            • "+ Create" beside a selector, from the device's own GUI; dialog tables in SATOM's table format. Request: "that same section has the pencil to create and you did not put it; are you using the crawler to scan everything? and check all those tables, the CSS does not match SATOM's format." FortiWeb offers Create inside the dropdown of every selector whose GUI source is declared createNew (204 of 220 sources on 7.6.8). The harvester now carries that flag from the GUI's own registry (harvester 5232929, knowledge pack kb-20261101.6: 119 templates, only the flag added), and SATOM draws a + beside each such selector (a native select has no room inside its list). It opens the object's empty dialog in a panel; on save the panel closes and the new object is selected (measured on {device}: a Trigger Policy created from Edit Signature Policy, then deleted). The signature categories' Trigger Policy column has it too. The tables inside FortiWeb-layout dialogs (sub-tables, HTTP Protocol Constraints, signature categories, toggle rows, the change review) now use SATOM's table format: uppercase secondary headers, no cell grid, zebra rows, a card around the large tables.
            • Edit Signature Policy draws its ten categories even when the policy has no rows; Signature Details slides in over the dialog. Request: "the table is empty in SATOM; Signature Details goes to another page while FortiWeb opens it as a side window; the signature types menu is collapsible." A signature policy created over the REST API has no main_class_list rows (lab-sr-01 to lab-sr-06 on {device}), so the dialog drew the table header with nothing under it. FortiWeb's dialog fills every missing category with Alert, High, disabled, False Positive Mitigation disabled, 600 s and no trigger (fwb-signature-dialog.js, 7.6.8); SATOM now does the same, in the dialog and in Signature Details. Such a category is written only if you change it, and then it is created with its whole row and its main_class_id (a PUT on a row that does not exist fails), with a dry run first and a re-read after (measured on {device} 7.6.8: created and verified, then removed). Signature Details now slides in from the right over the dialog in a wide panel instead of leaving it; Back to Signatures closes the panel, and a change written there reloads the dialog under it. Dictionaries folds as FortiWeb's tree does: categories with sub-categories open collapsed, each with an expand control; the pane itself folds away (chevron) and comes back. A right-click on a category or sub-category offers Enable and Disable, as on the device (a category: its row's status; a sub-category: sub_class_disable_list).
            • Signature Details as FortiWeb lays it out. Request: "do everything, leave nothing pending." The Signature Details button of Edit Signature Policy now opens the policy's Signature Details page (it opened the generic object editor), redrawn in the device's three panes: Dictionaries on the left (main category -> sub-category with this policy's status; a category without sub-categories is one entry listing its signatures; then Search and Filters), the selected entry in the middle (a main category's settings with Apply; a sub-category's signatures with Search Description; Search by CVE number, keywords or signature ID; Filters: Disabled, False Positive Mitigation Disabled, Alert Only, Exception) and the selected signature on the right (Signature, Exception, Threat Weight). Row menu: Enable, Disable in all policies, Disable in current policy. Sensitivity Level, Found In, Attack Reference, Match Example and Threat Weight are read from the device on Read from device (waf/signature.sigdetail, audited; only the pane's fields are kept; a refused read or an HTTP 200 without the signature is an error, never an empty pane). A CVE search without imported FortiGuard metadata says so. Back to Signatures returns to the dialog and only ever to a SATOM path. Disable in all policies writes a waf/base-signature-disable entry: the schema is measured (keyed by signature ID), the write round trip is not yet (unverified on this build).
            • Each selector lists what the device's GUI lists. 40 selectors of FortiWeb 7.6.8 dialogs were text boxes with no list and no Edit entry pencil (File List and Health Check trigger policies, the DoS and IP Protection exceptions, DLP rules and sensors, Trigger Policy's email / syslog / FortiAnalyzer / SIEM policies, report output policies...). The layouts now carry the source FortiWeb's code names for each one, resolved through the GUI's own registry (harvester a41df4a, knowledge pack kb-20261101.5): 180 pencils open the device's dialog, 4 the object editor. The measured list wins over SATOM's per-key map, which had Firewall Policy's Service listing server policy services instead of system/firewall.service. A GUI API list binds only to a twin SATOM measured. Five certificate selectors that FortiWeb filters by key type stay text boxes: SATOM cannot filter that list the same way and does not show a different one.
            • Help tips written with the lang filter are shown. 11 tips a build (Sensitivity Level among them) were dropped by the layout reader; they come with the layouts now.
            • Not in GUI, but in CLI follows the device's page. Where SATOM's schema-built page and a page of the device's GUI covered the same collection, the one that sorted first decided, and the schema-built page places every field: 14 collections listed nothing (Signatures, OCSP, ZTNA, Traffic Mirror, Padding Oracle, Web Vulnerability Scan...). The device's page decides now: Edit Signature Policy lists PII Hyperscan Mode, which FortiWeb's dialog never draws.
            • The Edit entry pencil opens the dialog the device draws. Request: "on the Web Protection Profile, the pencil on Signatures opens a screen that is not exactly what FortiWeb shows, and this happens in many places; clone exactly what is there and keep the help texts already added." The pencil beside a selector in a device-layout dialog used to open SATOM's generic object editor in the stacked panel; it now opens the referenced object in the dialog FortiWeb draws for it (146 selectors on FortiWeb 7.6.8; the generic editor stays the fallback where no page lists the collection, 3 today). The panel holds the dialog in a same-origin frame, so its own Save, live show/hide and pencils work there; Cancel and Esc close it. Only those dialog pages may be framed, and only by SATOM itself (X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN; every other page stays DENY).
            • Edit Signature Policy as on the device. Name, Custom Signature Group (with its list and Edit entry pencil), Sensitivity Level (with FortiWeb's tip) and Comments, then the signature classes table FortiWeb draws by hand: ten classes in the device's order with Status, False Positive Mitigation (SQL Injection rows only), Action (Information Disclosure and PII have their own choices), Block Period (only for a block-period action), Severity and Trigger Policy, and the PII Detection Threshold folded under its row; plus the Signature Details button. Changed classes are written row by row, dry run first. Rows SATOM cannot read are reported, never drawn empty.
            • Selectors the GUI crawl left unbound now list their objects. 38 selectors (Trigger Policy, exceptions, rules…) were drawn as text boxes with no list and no pencil; they take the collection the device schema names for the field. The remaining 40 stay text boxes until the crawl measures them (no guessed lists).
            • Web Protection pages drawn as FortiWeb draws them (FortiWeb 7.6.8). Request: "the Web Protection Profile page is not the same as on the FortiWeb; take that as the example but improve the WPP profiles, their exceptions and all of Web Protection, Bot Mitigation, API Protection, DoS Protection and IP Protection, identical in behaviour, menus and windows; use the harvester fully." The GUI was re-read with the harvester on a lab FortiWeb (50 pages) and the harvester's extractor and crawler were fixed where they lost what the device draws: section titles (the profile dialog has 15), the dialog's own notes, the collection each selector lists, the collection each sub-table lists, conditions that read a device object (Threat Score Profile shows only while threat scoring is enabled), the operation-mode and model rules (Waiting Room, Advanced Bot Protection), repeated method checkboxes and the row dialogs of tabbed pages. SATOM resolves those conditions from its cache, so fields appear and disappear as on the device.
            • HTTP Protocol Constraints: the profile's constraints in FortiWeb's table. The Edit dialog lists the 56 constraints in the device's seven collapsible categories, each with Status, Length (where the constraint has one), Action, Block Period, Severity, Threat Weight (0-5, as the device shows it), Trigger Policy and protocol support -- measured on the device's own dialog -- instead of two stray number fields marked "conditional". Every cell edits its REST key through the same Save.
            • Exceptions: every type with a measured row dialog is authored in it. Cookie Security, File Exception, Allow Method, Bot Mitigation, URL Encryption and Link Cloaking exceptions (and the others as the device exposes them) take FortiWeb's own fields, order, choices and conditions, including fields the old form lacked (Cookie Wildcard). A type with no measured dialog keeps the field list.
            • Exceptions: an HTTP Protocol Constraints exception is authored the way FortiWeb draws it. Request: "on {device} HTTP constraints is far more polished and easy to use; here the user does not know what it depends on or which parameters there are." The layout was measured in the device GUI ({device}, 7.6.8): Host Status / Host (greyed while off), Source IP / range (shown while on), URL Type as Simple String / Regular Expression, URL Pattern, then the 44 constraints in FortiWeb's seven collapsible categories with the device's names and descriptions. A column says, for the chosen Web Protection Profile, whether each constraint is ON in its HTTP Protocol Constraints profile (an exception for one that is off changes nothing), read from the SATOM cache. The one key the GUI does not show (Internal-resource-limits-check) sits under "Not in GUI, but in CLI".
            • Signature ID is picked from a list. Request: "Signature ID should be a select; nobody knows those by heart — open a modal with the signature id and everything it is, and pick it from there." Browse… opens the signature index (all of it, paged) with search and an attack-class filter; clicking a row fills the field.
            • Exceptions: the form says where Signature ID and HTTP Method come from. Request: "Signature ID — how will the user know which signature id to pick? And HTTP Method — where does that come from?" Signature ID now searches the local signature index as you type (id, attack class or description) and shows the picked signature's class and description, with a note that the value is the Attack log's Signature ID column. HTTP Method is a select of the device tokens (GET … OTHERS, read from the 7.6.8 and 8.0.6 CLI tree) instead of free text, still shown only for Element Type = HTTP Method.

            Fixed

            • Sentinel under-rated FortiWeb 7.6.8 attacks. The attack log on 7.6.8 writes threat_level as a word (Critical, Moderate), not a number (measured on {device}). Sentinel only read the numeric form, so an IP-list block the device rated Critical was stored as low and scored 24 points too low. The word is now read too (FortiWeb's own Informative and Substantial levels included), and the worse of the two severities still wins. Events already stored keep the severity they were stored with.

            • The catalog's child tables are measured, and three were wrong. Every child (sub-table) entry of the FortiWeb catalog was a legacy guess never measured on a device. All of them were probed on {device} 7.6.8 (GET the child with an existing parent): 95 answer as sub-tables and are now measured evidence (manual evidence 113; baseline promoted and re-sealed: 391 measured, 97 legacy left -- those have no parent object on the lab to probe). Three answered the PARENT object (FortiWeb ignores an unknown suffix), so whatever SATOM read or wrote there went to the wrong place: waf/graphql-validation.policy/graphql-rule-list, waf/site-publish-helper.policy/rule and waf/site-publish-helper.form-based-delegation/additional-field-list are the real ones (CLI schema and the GUI's member dialogs agree). The shipped baseline carries them, so a fresh installation gets them too. A second pass measured the children that had no parent object on the lab, without creating any (GET the child with a parent that does not exist: 200 with a list = a served sub-table, 500 errcode -3 = not a sub-table path; calibrated on a known-good and an invented path): 41 more are served; 15 legacy child entries are not paths FortiWeb serves at all (xml-exempted-urls/url-list, dlp.exception/exception-list, base-signature-disable/signature-list... -- none used by code) and left the catalog as measured absent; 19 sub-tables the GUI writes and the catalog lacked are registered (traffic-mirror/mirror-rule, ztna-profile/rule-list, waiting-room-policy/bypass-rules, the Site Publish pools' members, dlp.sensor/entries...). The dependency map clones those three new children and its four wrong child paths are fixed. Baseline: 451 measured, 42 legacy (was 296 / 192).

            • An object just created opens in its dialog (no more "Page not found"). A Custom Signature Group created with the "+" of Edit Signature Policy landed on the device, but its pencil answered "Page not found": SATOM cached a new FortiWeb object only when that type already had a cached object, and the dialog read the cache alone. The first object of a table the last sync read empty is now cached under that table's section (as FortiADC already was), and a dialog whose object is not cached yet reads that one object from the device; one the device does not have is still "not found".

            • Every writer caches the first object of an empty table, and the Audit Log names what a create created. Request: "this must never happen, we have to solve it always; and if it is in the log, why don't I see this insertion?" The empty-table fallback of the previous fix lived in one caller only: the object editor, FortiAuthenticator and FortiADC writes still left the first object of an empty table out of SATOM's copy. It now lives in the one function every writer uses. And every create was audited as mkey=None (a create's request names no object), so searching the Audit Log for the new object's name found nothing: the line now carries the object's own name (FortiWeb: from the payload; FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator, FortiADC, FortiAnalyzer: the key the re-read found) and two new fields, verify (what the re-read of the device found: verified, mismatch, unverified) and cache (what happened to SATOM's copy). The line is written after the re-read, so it states what the device holds. Earlier entries keep what they recorded.
            • A refused device read is no longer an empty signature policy. The class table and Signature Details read the policy's lists through a call that dropped the error: a 401 or a licence lock read as "no rows" (an empty table) or as "every signature enabled". A refusal now falls back to the SATOM cache; with nothing cached the dialog says so with the device's answer, the Dictionaries status reads unknown, and the signature search returns the error instead of rows.
            • Signatures disabled in all policies show as such. Signature Details read the waf/base-signature-disable entries by their cache key, which is the sequence id FortiWeb gives each entry (1, 2...), so no signature ever matched; it now reads each entry's signature_id. The Disable in all policies write is measured on {device} 7.6.8 (create, present on the device, delete) and is no longer marked unverified on this build.
            • A device registered while its REST API was licence-locked kept an empty firmware, and the GUI pages took the version from the model typed by hand (a 7.6.8 box was drawn with the 8.0.6 layout and the page said "This device runs 8.0.6"). The hourly device sync now re-reads the firmware when it was never read or is older than 6 hours, and a version that comes from the model on record is labelled as such.
            • Reference lists are served from the cache first. Every selector of a dialog asked the device on each open (42 calls for a Web Protection Profile); the device is asked only when the cache has nothing.
            • The device sync caches the GUI's own visibility map (system/state), which carries facts the configuration does not (Advanced Bot Protection on an unlicensed VM).
            • A signature exception built from the Attack log carried the method as the log prints it (GET); FortiWeb stores get. It is now lower-cased, like the Allow Method exception already was.
            • Exceptions: no gap between the Purge and Detect cards.
